violated_contract: After a credential revocation reports success, no request may authenticate with that credential. Developer and MCP API-key revocation deleted the positive Redis auth-cache entry and then the authoritative Firestore record; an authentication that read the still-existing record in between wrote the cache entry back with its one-hour TTL, so a key the owner had successfully revoked kept authenticating (and MCP auth could re-create its memory grant) until the entry expired.
canonical_prevention: Fence revocation with a durable deny marker that is written and acknowledged before any positive cache entry is purged or the authoritative record is deleted, and make every positive-cache fill atomic with a check of that marker, so cache hits, misses and in-flight fills all observe the revocation. When the marker cannot be read, authenticate from the authoritative record only and neither read nor fill the cache. Reversing the delete order alone does not close the interleaving.
